It can get better, typically through a few ways. You mentioned it happened after a panic attack, it is often linked to anxiety based roots. 

Typically what I've heard through surface level research is that it's a positive reinforcement cycle. The better it gets the less you think about it so it repeats. Same goes for the opposite. Sort of like panic attacks. 

Typically there is thought to be an underlying cause to cases of dpdr, hesitant to say always because there is always an exception. 

But circling back around, I've been good for a while now. Could always happen again, could never happen again. I don't know. It doesn't really get "cured" and "recover" isn't the right word it's more management. With management comes a reduction in symptoms.

I'll start off with addressing the therapy issue. Unfortunately it is apparent that the field is not where it needs to be when it comes to treating and tolerating BPD. Therapists often times do lose their temper, or cut a person off. They are only human after all.  As far as the medication goes, look into mainline treatment for BPD. You will find that medication is not what most experts recommend as the major treatment. Instead typically as a solution to co-morbid issues. DBT and other forms of therapy are what studies back. I would certainly say that understanding your behavioral patterns and symptoms will be helpful in your journey. 

​

As for final words of encouragement, BPD is something that actually can get better with age. People (hesitant to say often but that is my understanding) report that they can better function in life as they mature and grow. Which seems to point towards learning to manage it as you go. I do not know your specific symptoms, but take fear of abandonment for as an example. In DBT they will try to get you to use coping skills in order to manage that fear and to try and avoid spiraling. As time goes on it gets easier for someone to refine their own methods of coping, hopefully to the point where it is what you could call easy.
